metadata.document: NDPR Implementation Framework + NDP Act GAID 2025

clauses.title: Background & Objectives
clauses.summary: The NDP Act 2023 is Nigeria's primary data protection law, superseding the NDPR 2019. Per GAID Art. 3(3), the NDPR ceases to apply as a legal instrument upon GAID issuance. The Act safeguards the constitutional right to privacy under s.37 of the 1999 Constitution. It applies to all data controllers/processors in Nigeria and those targeting Nigerian data subjects (s.2).
clauses.penalty_info: Non-compliance can result in fines up to ₦10M or 2% of annual gross revenue, whichever is greater.

clauses.title: Material Context & Exemptions
clauses.summary: Exemptions under NDP Act s.3 apply to personal/household processing but even exempt activities must comply with: data protection principles (s.24), lawful bases (s.25), DPO designation (s.32), breach notification (s.40), and data subject rights (Part VI). Per GAID Art. 6, individuals who process data for personal purposes remain accountable if they put others' privacy at risk.
clauses.penalty_info: Misapplying exemptions does not shield from enforcement.

clauses.title: Compliance Framework & Registration
clauses.summary: Data controllers must: register with NDPC as data controller/processor of major importance (if processing 200+ subjects in 6 months), file annual Compliance Audit Returns (CAR) by March 31st, publish privacy policies on all platforms, designate a DPO, conduct DPIAs when required, notify NDPC of breaches within 72 hours, and train staff. Three classification levels: UHL (₦250,000), EHL (₦100,000), OHL (₦10,000). Late CAR filing incurs 50% penalty.
clauses.penalty_info: Registration fees: UHL ₦250,000, EHL ₦100,000, OHL ₦10,000. Late CAR filing: 50% administrative penalty.

clauses.title: Data Processing & DPIA
clauses.summary: DPIA is mandatory under GAID Art. 28 for: profiling/scoring, automated decision-making with legal effects, systematic monitoring, sensitive data, vulnerable data subjects, new technologies, financial services, healthcare, e-commerce, and surveillance cameras. Must be filed with NDPC. DPIA template provided in GAID Schedule 4 covers: nature of processing, lawful basis, necessity/proportionality, stakeholder consultation, vulnerabilities, and cross-border transfers.
clauses.penalty_info: Processing without lawful basis or required DPIA can trigger enforcement proceedings.

clauses.title: Consent & Lawful Bases
clauses.summary: Six lawful bases: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interest, public interest, legitimate interest. Consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous. No implied consent. Per GAID Art. 19, cookie banners must be conspicuous and obstruct the page — bottom placement is tantamount to lack of transparency. Children need guardian consent. GAID Art. 18 lists activities always requiring consent including marketing, sharing with third parties, and biometric processing.
clauses.penalty_info: Processing without valid consent or lawful basis is a direct violation subject to sanctions.

clauses.title: Data Protection Audit & CAR
clauses.article_ref: NDP Act s.6(d), GAID Art.10, Sch.2
clauses.summary: Annual Compliance Audit Returns (CAR) are mandatory for UHL/EHL data controllers. The CAR template in GAID Schedule 2 covers: governance (DPO, training, policies), technology (data security controls, access, encryption), accountability (DPIA, legitimate interest, ROPA), cross-border transfers, and data processors. UHL/EHL must file through a licensed DPCO. OHL must renew registration annually instead.
clauses.penalty_info: Late filing: 50% administrative penalty on filing fee. Non-filing triggers enforcement.

clauses.title: Cross-Border Data Transfer
clauses.article_ref: NDP Act Part VIII, GAID Art.45, Sch.5
clauses.summary: Cross-border transfers require: NDPC adequacy decision, approved Cross-Border Data Transfer Instrument (CBDTI — codes of conduct, certifications, BCR, or SCC), or valid lawful basis with safeguards. GAID Schedule 5 details adequacy assessment criteria: enforceable data subject rights, independent supervisory authority, effective data protection law, and international commitments. Data sovereignty considerations are mandatory.
clauses.penalty_info: Unauthorized cross-border transfers subject to enforcement and possible prosecution.

clauses.title: Data Retention & Storage
clauses.summary: Per NDP Act s.24(1)(d), data must not be retained longer than necessary. GAID Art. 49(3) specifies: where no timebound obligation exists, storage lapses 6 months after the original purpose is accomplished. Data subjects can request deletion. Data no longer needed must be destroyed. A clear data retention policy must be communicated to data subjects.
clauses.penalty_info: Improper retention can constitute a breach subject to enforcement.

clauses.title: Data Breach Notification
clauses.summary: Per NDP Act s.40(2) and GAID Art. 33, breaches must be reported to NDPC within 72 hours. Data subjects must be notified immediately if the breach poses high risk (risk of fraud, identity theft, or exposure of sensitive data). Notification must include: breach circumstances, timeline, affected data description, risk assessment, estimated affected individuals, mitigation steps, and DPO contact. Immediate notification to all relevant authorities is required for national-scale breaches.
clauses.penalty_info: Failure to report breaches within 72 hours triggers enforcement and possible prosecution.

clauses.title: Enforcement & Penalties
clauses.article_ref: NDP Act Part X, GAID Art.48
clauses.summary: NDPC enforces through: surveillance, complaint filing, investigation, administrative sanctions, and criminal prosecution. Compliance evidence (registration, CAR filing, DPIA submission) shows prima facie good faith but does not replace concrete evidence of compliance. Fines based on: nature/gravity of breach, number of affected subjects, damage suffered, and repeat offence status.
clauses.penalty_info: Fines up to ₦10M or 2% of annual gross revenue. Criminal prosecution possible.

clauses.title: Data Subject Rights
clauses.article_ref: NDP Act Part VI, GAID Art.36-40
clauses.summary: Data subjects have rights to: rectification (GAID Art. 36 — cannot require affidavit if aligning with NIN), portability (Art. 37 — applies where consent/contract basis), erasure/right to be forgotten (Art. 38), and lodging complaints with NDPC (Art. 39). GAID Schedule 9 provides a Standard Notice to Address Grievance (SNAG) template. Controllers must design systems for seamless data requests.
clauses.penalty_info: Failure to facilitate data subject rights is an enforceable violation.

clauses.title: Third Party Processing & DPA
clauses.summary: Per GAID Art. 34, Data Processing Agreements must include: party details, purpose, location, lawful bases, scope, technical/organisational measures, DPIA outcomes, confidentiality, tenure, indemnity, insurance, and dispute resolution. Controllers are liable for processor violations. Processors of major importance must register with NDPC. Sub-processor compliance must be verified.
clauses.penalty_info: Controller liable for third-party processor violations without proper DPA.

clauses.title: DPO Designation & Credential Assessment
clauses.summary: DPO designation is mandatory for data controllers/processors of major importance. Per GAID Art. 12, DPOs must: be actively engaged in all data processing issues, receive adequate resources and training, report directly to management, and not face dismissal for performing duties. GAID Art. 13 requires DPOs to prepare semi-annual data protection reports. Annual Credential Assessment (ACA) per GAID Art. 14 and Schedule 3 scores DPOs on certification, training hours, examination, and CPD credits.
clauses.penalty_info: Failure to designate a qualified DPO is an enforceable violation.

clauses.title: Cross-Border Transfer Instruments
clauses.summary: For non-adequacy countries, NDPC may approve Cross-Border Data Transfer Instruments (CBDTI): codes of conduct, certifications, binding corporate rules, or standard contractual clauses. Special circumstances (jural/fiduciary) allow transfers for: defence of legal claims, vital interest, public interest, and data subject consent with proper risk communication. Data sovereignty is a key consideration.
clauses.penalty_info: NDPC can prohibit transfers and initiate prosecution.

clauses.title: Capacity Building & Training
clauses.summary: Per GAID Art. 30, data controllers must prepare and follow schedules for internal sensitisation and training on privacy (SToP). All employees must be trained within 6 months of business commencement and at least annually thereafter. GAID Art. 46 makes capacity building mandatory as an organisational measure. A Basic Privacy Checklist (BPC) must be developed for all staff.
clauses.penalty_info: Lack of staff training cited as aggravating factor in enforcement.

clauses.title: Data Ethics & Emerging Technologies
clauses.summary: GAID Art. 41-44 address data ethics and emerging technologies (AI, IoT, Blockchain). Key requirements: DPIA mandatory before deploying ETs, automated profiling must not lead to prejudiced outcomes, third-party data sharing requires explicit consent, data subjects have the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions. Data Subject Vulnerability Indexes (DSVI in Schedule 6) must be considered: age, health, financial difficulty, disability, and digital literacy.
clauses.penalty_info: Non-compliant use of emerging technologies triggers enforcement under the NDP Act.

clauses.title: Software Deployment & Privacy by Design
clauses.summary: Per GAID Art. 31, deploying data processing software (mobile apps, operating systems, firmware, etc.) requires: DPIA before deployment, privacy by design and by default, privacy policy within the software, privacy statement before installation detailing data types, purposes, encryption, and self-service uninstall options. Existing software must be updated within 6 months of GAID issuance.
clauses.penalty_info: Non-compliant software deployment is an enforceable violation.

clauses.title: Data Security & Monitoring
clauses.summary: Per GAID Art. 29, data controllers must prepare Monitoring, Evaluation and Maintenance (MEM) schedules for data security systems. Security must address: Volume, Value, Veracity, Velocity and Variety of data. Technical measures include: encryption at rest/in transit, multi-factor authentication, anti-ransomware/malware, access controls. GAID Schedule 2 Part 2 rates security from Poor to Industry Grade (ISO 27000, NIST, CIS, COBIT).
clauses.penalty_info: Inadequate security measures trigger enforcement proceedings.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Does your app collect personal data (names, emails, phone numbers)?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Collecting personal data triggers NDP Act compliance requirements including registration with NDPC, privacy policies, consent mechanisms, and annual compliance audits.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you store health, biometric, or other sensitive personal data?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Sensitive personal data requires explicit consent and a mandatory DPIA under GAID Art. 28. Health apps and fintech are classified as high-risk sectors.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you have a published privacy policy on your app/website?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Per GAID Art. 7(j-k), you must publish a compliant privacy policy on all platforms where data processing occurs. Cookie/privacy notices must be conspicuous.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you transfer user data outside Nigeria (e.g., cloud hosting abroad)?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Cross-border transfers require NDPC adequacy decision or approved CBDTI per NDP Act Part VIII and GAID Art. 45.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you have a process to obtain explicit user consent before data collection?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Per GAID Art. 17, consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous. Pre-ticked boxes and bundled consent are prohibited.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Does your app target users under 13 years old?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Processing children's data requires guardian consent and child-friendly privacy notices. GAID Art. 43 requires DSVI consideration for minors.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you share user data with third-party services (analytics, payment processors)?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Per GAID Art. 34, all third-party processors need Data Processing Agreements covering purpose, security measures, and DPIA outcomes.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Do you have a data breach notification process (72-hour reporting to NDPC)?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Per NDP Act s.40 and GAID Art. 33, breaches must be reported to NDPC within 72 hours with detailed incident information.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Are you registered with NDPC as a data controller or processor of major importance?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Per GAID Art. 8-9, organisations processing 200+ data subjects in 6 months must register with NDPC. Classification: UHL, EHL, or OHL.

risk_scanner_questions.question: Does your app use AI, automated decision-making, or profiling?
risk_scanner_questions.explanation: Per GAID Art. 43, deploying emerging technologies requires DPIA, DSVI assessment, safeguards against discriminatory profiling, and privacy by design.

questions.text: Is the organisation currently registered with NDPC as a data controller/processor of major importance?
Is there a designated Data Protection Officer (DPO) for the organisation?
Is the DPO certified and enrolled on the NDPC database with valid credentials?
Does the DPO prepare and submit Semi-Annual Data Protection Reports to management?
Does the organisation have a schedule for capacity building on data protection for all employees?
Has the organisation developed a Basic Privacy Checklist (BPC) for all staff?
Does the organisation have a Monitoring, Evaluation and Maintenance (MEM) schedule for data security?
Is the organisational privacy policy published on all platforms where data processing occurs?
Is a conspicuous cookie notice displayed on the homepage (not at the bottom)?
Has the organisation filed its annual Compliance Audit Returns (CAR) by March 31st?
Does the DPO report directly to management and have adequate resources?
Has the DPO obtained required Continuous Professional Development Credits within 12 months?
For UHL/EHL organisations, is CAR filed through a licensed DPCO?
Has the organisation carefully assessed and documented its lawful bases for all processing activities?
Is consent obtained through clear, specific, freely given mechanisms (no pre-ticked boxes)?
Is the cookie consent banner conspicuous and not placed at the bottom of the page?
If relying on legitimate interest, has a Legitimate Interest Assessment been conducted?
Has a DPIA been conducted for high-risk processing (profiling, sensitive data, new tech, etc.)?
For deployed software, was a DPIA conducted before deployment with privacy by design?
Are data security measures regularly evaluated using MEM schedules?
Is there a documented breach notification process with 72-hour NDPC reporting?
Are cross-border transfers based on NDPC adequacy decisions or approved CBDTI?
Do all third-party processors have compliant Data Processing Agreements?
Has the organisation verified that third-party processors are registered with NDPC?
If using AI/IoT/Blockchain, has a DPIA been conducted with DSVI assessment?
Has testing been conducted in low-risk environments before full deployment?
Are there safeguards against discriminatory profiling and disparate outcomes?

classification_thresholds.UHL: 5,000+ data subjects in 6 months or specific sectors (banks, telecoms, fintechs, oil & gas, etc.)
classification_thresholds.EHL: 1,000-5,000 data subjects in 6 months or MDAs, micro-finance banks, higher institutions, hospitals
classification_thresholds.OHL: 200-1,000 data subjects in 6 months or primary schools, primary health centres, small hotels
